summary: Network facts modules (eos_facts, ios_facts, vyos_facts) use inventory credentials and store results as ansible_net_* facts; tasks run conditionally by ansible_network_os.
questions: What facts do network facts modules return?
How do I get the OS version of a switch with Ansible?
How do I run the right facts module for each platform?

answer_card.title: Network facts modules
answer_card.answer_md: Modules like `arista.eos.eos_facts`, `cisco.ios.ios_facts` and `vyos.vyos.vyos_facts` use inventory credentials and store results as facts prefixed `ansible_net_` (for example `ansible_net_version`, `ansible_net_hostname`). See each module's Return Values. Run the matching module with `when: ansible_network_os == '...'`.
